title: Multi-aggregate expected-version commit in SqliteEventStore
description:
Filed by architect-bdaffeaf 2026-08-20 from worker-e194c5f6's measured stop (comment-4874573b on task-e194c5f6, HEAD 0c32df9) — the prerequisite that unblocks the atomic budget-reservation-during-activation composition.

MEASURED GAP (decisive, six clauses in the source comment): CommitExpectedVersionDecisionInput carries ONE targetAggregateId (store-contracts.ts:83) and ONE expectedVersion (:80); EventDraft has NO aggregate field (:36-44); event-ledger-append.ts inserts one aggregate_id (:92-131) and upserts one aggregate_heads row (:214-216). Budget and activation aggregates are DISTINCT by derivation (deriveBudgetAggregateId vs deriveActivationAggregateId) with INCOMPATIBLE version fences (activation pins EXPECTED_VERSION=0; budget passes current.headVersion). Two decisions under one commandId refuse (BUDGET_LEDGER_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT on foreign commandKind); a derived second commandId is the compensating-commit shape the budget rails forbid; the in-transaction commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply seam would force hand-written domain_events/aggregate_heads in the daemon — forbidden by every module contract.

DELIVERABLE: a public @moe/store multi-leg commit — ONE decision, per-leg {aggregateId, expectedVersion, events[]} in the ONE existing transaction, per-leg getAggregateVersion fencing, all-or-nothing (any leg's version race refuses the whole commit with the store's existing refusal vocabulary extended minimally), replay identity unchanged (same command bytes → original decision, zero new events on ANY leg). No schema change beyond what the leg loop needs; the single-aggregate path stays byte-identical in behavior.

CONSUMER (clause 1a): task-e194c5f6 (BLOCKED naming this gap) — its step 4 resumes the moment this lands. Do NOT widen: no cross-project legs, no partial-success mode, no new event table.
definitionOfDone: A public @moe/store commit accepts ordered legs {aggregateId, expectedVersion, events[]} under ONE decision key and commits all legs in the ONE existing SQLite transaction; any leg's expected-version mismatch refuses the WHOLE commit with an exact stable code naming the failing leg's aggregate, and zero rows persist on any leg
Same-byte replay returns the original decision with raw event/decision counts unchanged on EVERY leg; conflicting bytes under the same key refuse with the first record intact
The existing single-aggregate commit path is behavior-identical: its suites pass unmodified, and a byte-compat pin test proves an unchanged commit produces identical rows

Real file-backed SqliteEventStore tests cover a two-leg accepted control (distinct aggregates, distinct expected versions), each leg's version-race refusal, replay, and a mutation drill where splitting the transaction into two commits reds a named atomicity test
packages/store test + typecheck legs exit 0 with nonzero count lines; every production source <=250 physical lines; completion records task-e194c5f6 as the consumer
taskRails: Extend, never fork: the leg loop lives inside the existing transaction/append path (event-ledger-append/transaction); no daemon-side raw SQL, no second commit entry point, no partial success
Preserve the store's existing refusal codes and replay identity semantics; new codes only where no existing one names the condition, and the failing LEG must be identifiable from the refusal
TDD; target <=250 lines per production source; commit only explicit owned paths in packages/store

Read the decision ROW shape (CommandDecisionRecordBase :86+, businessEventIds) and the replay/idempotency read path (command-decision suites name it) — the multi-leg commit must keep the decision row shape compatible enough that existing readers (getCommandDecision/getCommandReceipt consumers repo-wide) do not change; measure what receipt fields (eventIds, aggregateId, currentVersion/previousVersion) mean for a multi-leg commit and DECIDE + record: receipt carries the PRIMARY leg's aggregate plus per-leg detail, or a new receipt variant — the choice must not break the foundation-context strict reader's receipt proofs (225d25f7's suite pins previousVersion/currentVersion/eventIds semantics — grep its assertions before deciding). implementationPlan.description: TDD RED — NEW packages/store/src/command-decision-multi-leg.test.ts (colocated with the command-decision suites; real file-backed store closed in finally). Against a not-yet-existing public commit (working name commitExpectedVersionDecisionLegs; input {commandKind, committedResultBytes, correlationId, decidedAt, key, requestBytes, legs: [{aggregateId, expectedVersion, events}]}): (a) TWO-LEG ACCEPTED CONTROL: distinct aggregates at distinct versions (leg A a fresh aggregate at 0, leg B an existing aggregate at head N) — one decision row, every leg's events inserted with correct sequence, both aggregate_heads advanced; assert raw per-aggregate event counts and head versions BY READING BACK; (b) ALL-OR-NOTHING: leg B's expectedVersion stale (concurrent bump between read and commit) → the WHOLE commit refuses with an exact stable code NAMING the failing leg's aggregateId; assert ZERO rows persisted on leg A too (read back both aggregates — the atomicity assertion IS the task); (c) REPLAY: same-byte replay returns the original decision with counts unchanged on EVERY leg; conflicting bytes under the same key refuse with the first record intact; (d) SINGLE-LEG EQUIVALENCE: a one-leg call behaves exactly like the existing single-aggregate commit (same decision row shape, same receipt) — assert against the EXISTING API's output on identical inputs (byte-compat by comparison, not by claim); (e) BOUNDS: zero legs refuses; duplicate aggregateId across legs refuses (two version fences on one head is incoherent — pinned code); leg-count bound at-limit accept + one-over refuse; (f) receipt semantics per the step-1 decision, pinned. Run: RED.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (a) Daemon-side two commits with a derived second commandId — already rejected by the budget rails (compensating commit) and the blocking worker's own analysis; this task exists because that door is closed. (b) Using commitExpectedVersionDecisionWithApply from the daemon — rejected: hand-writing domain_events/aggregate_heads outside the store violates every module contract (the worker's clause 6). (c) A new parallel commit entry with its own transaction code — rejected by rail 1 (extend, never fork): the leg loop lives inside the existing transaction/append internals so rollback discipline and prepared statements stay single-sourced. (d) Partial success / per-leg outcomes — explicitly out of scope: all-or-nothing is the entire point. (e) Unifying the single-leg path through the new loop — allowed ONLY if byte-compat holds by comparison test; otherwise parallel internals with the divergence noted.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MAPPED at filing (HEAD post-0c32df9): the commit path is facade (sqlite-event-store.ts:261-271, 381 lines — already past the 250 target, 400 hard cap is the live risk) → core (decision-ledger.ts:93/:110-115) → atomic transaction (decision-ledger-transaction.ts, BEGIN IMMEDIATE :117, rollback normalization :207-216) → append internals (event-ledger-append.ts, prepared insertEvent :42/:91, aggregate_heads upsert :214-216). The single-aggregate constraint is exactly worker-e194c5f6's six-clause measurement (comment-4874573b): input carries one targetAggregateId/expectedVersion (store-contracts.ts:74-84), EventDraft has no aggregate field, one heads row per commit. getAggregateVersion exists (:278) for per-leg fencing. THE SUBTLE CONSUMER CONSTRAINT: CommandReceipt semantics (previousVersion/currentVersion/eventIds/aggregateId) are PINNED by the 225d25f7 strict foundation-context reader's decision/receipt proofs — the multi-leg receipt decision must not break those; step 1 forces the measurement + recorded decision before any type is written. The WithApply in-transaction escape hatch stays untouched (it is the hand-written-SQL hazard the blocking worker refused).
planningNotes.risks: (1) sqlite-event-store.ts at 381: any nontrivial facade addition risks the 400 hard cap — split-first is pre-authorized with the count recorded. (2) node:sqlite forbids nested transactions — the leg loop must reuse the ONE BEGIN IMMEDIATE; every new throw path must land in the existing rollback normalization. (3) Receipt compatibility is the hidden repo-wide contract — the 225d25f7 suite is the canary; run it by name. (4) The prepared insertEvent/heads statements are per-connection state — threading aggregateId per leg must not rebuild statements per leg (perf + the existing reuse pattern). (5) Replay identity excludes event bytes (standing gotcha) — the conflicting-bytes arm must present materially different requestBytes, and per-leg counts are the idempotence assertion, not verdicts. (6) Shared worktree: store package is otherwise quiet; pathspec commits.
